recreation_brief: 1. Set slide background to white. 2. Place a yellow oval at the top-right corner with the text '32' in black. 3. On the left side, create four rectangular boxes with red outlines stacked vertically with small gaps. Label them 'Threshold=0.0', 'Threshold=0.1', 'Threshold=0.3', 'Threshold=0.4' in red text at the top of each box. 4. Inside each box, draw a 2x2 table. Add 'Predicted as' above the columns with headers 'P' and 'N'. Add 'Actual' to the left of the rows with labels 'P' and 'N'. Fill cells: Threshold 0.0 -> 5,0 / 6,0; Threshold 0.1 -> 5,0 / 4,2; Threshold 0.3 -> 5,0 / 2,4; Threshold 0.4 -> 4,1 / 1,5. 5. To the right of each matrix, add two lines of black text: for 0.0 'TPR=5/(5+0)=1' and 'FPR=6/(6+0)=1'; for 0.1 'TPR=5/(5+0)=1' and 'FPR=4/(4+2)=.66'; for 0.3 'TPR=5/(5+0)=1' and 'FPR=2/(2+4)=.33'; for 0.4 'TPR=4/(4+1)=4/5' and 'FPR=1/(1+5)=.16'. 6. In the center-bottom area, add a red-outlined rectangle with centered black text 'ROC Curve for Same Model -different thresholds'. 7. On the right-top, draw a square plot area with light gray grid lines. Add a vertical y-axis labeled 'TPR' with an upward arrow and a horizontal x-axis labeled 'FPR' with a rightward arrow. Plot four red circles at coordinates (0.33,1.0), (0.66,1.0), (1.0,1.0), and (0.16,0.8). Connect them with a red line in order from lower-left to upper-right. Label each point with its threshold value: '0.3', '0.1', '0.0', '0.4'. 8. On the right-bottom, add the formula 'TPR = TP/(TP+FN)' with TP over TP+FN as a fraction, and 'FPR = FP/(FP+TN)' with FP over FP+TN as a fraction. Below the formulas, draw a 2x2 legend table with 'Predicted as' header (P, N), 'Actual' row labels (P, N), and cells TP, FN, FP, TN. Fill the TP and TN cells with light green.
